answer: An orchard keeper defends an agent economy with a ladder of puzzles recorded in one shared atlas: every new identity must solve a puzzle whose answer starts with one more zero than the last, so the first fake searches about 16 tries, the second 256, the third 4,096, the tenth about 1.1 trillion and the twentieth about 1.2 quintillion. Bulk farming fails because each puzzle is chained to the hash of the identity before it, so no puzzle can be solved early, in parallel, or bought ready-made; each agent climbs the ladder alone, and only a haven of honest agents survives the climb.
